title: Feedback-enabled magnomechanics in lithium ferrite
authors: Mehri Ebrahimi, Yunhu Huang, Ali Rashedi, John P. Davis
abstract: Lithium ferrite (LiFe) is a promising material for cavity magnonics because its large spin density enables strong coupling between magnons and microwave photons. Its potential for cavity magnomechanics, however, has remained unexplored. Here, we observe magnomechanical interactions in a single-crystal LiFe sphere using coherent microwave feedback to suppress dissipation of the cavity--magnon polariton. In the absence of sufficient feedback, the narrow mechanical response is difficult to resolve against the much broader polariton background. Increasing the feedback gain reduces the polariton linewidth and correspondingly increases the magnomechanical cooperativity, revealing a clear magnomechanically induced transparency feature. In the measurements presented here, the effective upper-polariton linewidth is reduced from $3.53~\mathrm{MHz}$ without feedback to $5.8~\mathrm{kHz}$ in the presence of feedback, while the measured cooperativity increases from $C=1.9\times10^{-3}$ to $C=0.15$. These measurements provide, to our knowledge, the first observation of cavity magnomechanics in LiFe and demonstrate coherent feedback as a practical route for accessing weak interactions that would otherwise be obscured by dissipation.
summary: This paper reports the first observation of cavity magnomechanics in Lithium ferrite (LiFe) by utilizing coherent microwave feedback. The feedback technique is crucial because it suppresses cavity dissipation, dramatically increasing the measurable cooperativity. This allows the researchers to quantify the weak magnomechanical coupling in LiFe, demonstrating a powerful method for probing subtle quantum interactions.
main_problem: The primary challenge was observing and characterizing the weak magnomechanical coupling in Lithium ferrite (LiFe) when the mechanical signal was otherwise obscured by cavity dissipation.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated cavity magnomechanics in LiFe using coherent microwave feedback, significantly increasing the measurable cooperativity and revealing a clear magnomechanically induced transparency feature.
method: The technique involves implementing coherent microwave feedback into the cavity to suppress polariton dissipation, thereby enhancing the detectability of the weak mechanical interaction.
model_or_system: The system uses a single-crystal LiFe sphere coupled to a microwave cavity, exhibiting cavity magnonics and cavity magnomechanics. The dynamics are analyzed using cavity field equations modified by the feedback loop.
key_observables: Polariton linewidth ($	ilde{\kappa}_{\pm}$), Magnomechanical Cooperativity ($C$), and the Magnomechanically Induced Transparency (MMIT) feature.
important_parameters: The single-magnon coupling rate ($g_{mb}/2\pi$) for LiFe ($0.26 	ext{ mHz}$) and the enhancement factor provided by the feedback gain ($g_{fb}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that coherent feedback can effectively engineer the cavity dissipation to reveal underlying weak coupling mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the avoided crossing defining polariton branches, the feedback setup, and crucially, show the MMIT feature becoming resolvable as the microwave feedback gain increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system, details the necessity and implementation of coherent microwave feedback, presents quantitative measurements showing the enhancement of cooperativity and the resolution of the MMIT feature, and concludes with a comparison of the coupling strength between LiFe and YIG.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses active dissipation engineering (feedback) to access and quantify weak coupling regimes, a core theme in open quantum systems and cavity QED.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Normalized transmission spectrum |S21| as a function of bias magnetic field B0, showing the avoided crossing between the cavity and magnon modes. The resulting upper and lower branches correspond to the hybridized cavity–magnon polariton modes.

FIG. 2. (a) Schematic of the cavity magnomechanical system and microwave feedback loop. The LiFe sphere is positioned inside a copper microwave cavity and probed by a vector network analyzer (VNA). A fraction of the cavity output is routed through the feed- back loop, where the signal is amplified, phase shifted, and subse- quently fed back into the cavity. An independent microwave source provides the drive tone for the magnomechanical measurements. (b) Frequency schematic of the measurement showing the drive tone, ωd, approximately one mechanical frequency, ωb, red-detuned from the upper-polariton mode, ω+.

FIG. 3. Transmission amplitude |S21| of the upper polariton mea- sured without feedback at a drive power of 25 dBm. The expanded view in the upper reveals the weak magnomechanical feature near the mechanical resonance, which is barely detectable against the broader upper-polariton response.

FIG. 4. Feedback-enabled observation of magnomechanically in- duced transparency in LiFe. Normalized transmission |S21| is shown as a function of probe detuning ∆sd = ωs −ωd for increasing feed- back gain gfb (bottom to top), with constant pump tone power, Pd = 22.6dBm. The feedback suppresses the upper-polariton linewidth from κ+/2π = 3.53 MHz without feedback to ˜κ+/2π = 33.8 kHz and 5.8 kHz at feedback gains gfb = 28.12 dB and 31.75 dB, respec- tively, while increasing the extracted magnomechanical cooperativity from C = 1.9×10−3 without feedback to C = 0.02 and 0.15, respec- tively. FIG. 5. Effect of coherent feedback on the magnomechanical inter- action. (a) Extracted effective upper-polariton linewidth ˜κ+, drive- enhanced upper-polariton–phonon coupling rate G+, and mechani- cal linewidth κb as functions of the feedback gain gfb. Increasing the feedback gain strongly reduces ˜κ+, while G+ and κb remain com- paratively small. Dashed lines are guides to the eye. (b) Correspond- ing magnomechanical cooperativity C = G2+/( ˜κ+κb) as a function of feedback gain. The suppression of the upper-polariton linewidth results in a pronounced increase in the cooperativity. The dashed line is a guide to the eye.

Spintronics.note: The paper directly addresses cavity magnomechanics, which involves the coupling of magnons (spin waves) to a microwave cavity, fitting perfectly within the scope of magnon/photon polaritons and quantum-optical descriptions of magnetic systems.
